decisions.why: The glossary row conculcáre is open: *calcar aos pés* (90:13) against *pisar aos pés*, which Ps 7:6 took after *calque* was unknown to the blind reader and 'pouco corrente' to the stylist, and which the row now proposes. Ps 55 has the verb twice in two verses (κατεπάτησεν … κατεπάτησαν), so one verb serves both. *aos pés* kept: bare *pisar* can be heard as merely stepping on. MS1932 has both verbs (*me calcou aos pés … Pisaram-me*), DRB 'trodden me under foot … trodden on me'. **v2:** the stylist refused *pisar aos pés* in both verses as a crossed idiom and asked for *calcar aos pés*; taken — the Ps 7 readers stumbled on the rare form *calque*, while *calcou / calcaram* are current; the ambiguity reader passed *calcou*-family words without remark.

options.label: me calcou aos pés / Calcaram-me aos pés
options.note: Ruling (v2); stylist v1: *pisar aos pés* is two idioms crossed, *calcar aos pés* the set phrase; = 90:13 and MS1932. Ps 7:6's trouble was the subjunctive *calque*, not the idiom.

options.label: me pisou aos pés / Pisaram-me aos pés
options.note: Draft 1; the row's proposal after Ps 7:6.

options.label: me pisou / Pisaram-me
options.note: shorter; loses the trampling the con- gives.

decisions.why: The participle has no object in the Latin (πολεμῶν); *impugnáre → combater* as in 34:1 (*os que me combatem*); *tribuláre → atribular* (row). *tota die → o dia todo* (D24) first, as in the Latin, so it can go with either verb as it can there. The Lenten Gradual (Quad3-1, Quad5-1 by grep) sings this colon with *bellans* for *impúgnans*.

options.label: combatendo, me atribulou
options.note: Ruling; the participle without an object, as the Latin; the colon ends on the main verb, as the Latin.

options.label: combatendo-me, atribulou-me
options.note: DRB 'fighting against me'; supplies an object the Latin lacks, and two enclitics in a row.

options.label: me atribulou, combatendo
options.note: MS1932's order (*angustiou-me, combatendo*); cadence on a paroxytone.

decisions.why: *bellári* (only here in the psalter, grep) is 'to wage war'; the Greek πολεμοῦντες is the same verb as 55:2's πολεμῶν (*impúgnans* → *combater*), so D15's test would allow one Portuguese verb — but the Latin varies here, *combater* in both would drop *bellum*'s war, and Portuguese has a plain second verb. The copula *são* supplied (grammar, D2; MS1932 *porque são muitos os que pelejam*).

options.label: guerreiam
options.note: Ruling; keeps *bellum*; plain.

options.label: lutam
options.note: plainest; loses the war.

options.label: combatem
options.note: one verb with 55:2, as the Greek; the Latin varies.

options.label: pelejam
options.note: MS1932; dated in Brazilian speech.

decisions.why: A crux: the Latin (ἀπὸ ὕψους ἡμέρας) can be the height of the day (noon — DRB 'From the height of the day') or height as haughtiness; the Hebrew מָרוֹם belongs to 55:3 ('proudly'), which is where the Latin's reading comes from, and MS1932 turns it to dawn (*desde que desponta o dia*). The Latin is kept as it stands; *altitúdo → altura* is the open row's word (11:9, 68:3, 102:11). *desde* holds both time and place in Portuguese, as *ab* does. **v2:** the Latinist asked for plain *da*, which keeps *ab* as open as the Latin (time from which, or cause); taken.

options.label: Da altura do dia
options.note: Ruling (v2); latinist v1: *desde* makes *ab* only temporal; *da* keeps time, place and cause open.

options.label: Desde a altura do dia
options.note: Draft 1; DRB's reading, the row's word.

options.label: Do alto do dia
options.note: plainer noun; *do alto* leans to a place.

options.label: Desde que desponta o dia
options.note: MS1932; refused: it interprets (dawn), and the Latin says height.

decisions.latin: non timébo quid fáciat mihi caro / homo
decisions.why: The refrain's second half, and word for word Ps 117:6 *non timébo quid fáciat mihi homo* → *não temerei o que me faça o homem* (finished): identical Latin, identical Portuguese (rule 6). 55:5 differs only in *caro* → *a carne* (the flesh, kept concrete: 15:9, 27:7b); 55:11 is 117:6 exactly.

options.label: o que me faça
options.note: Ruling; = 117:6.

options.label: o que me possa fazer
options.note: MS1932; adds 'can'; would part from 117:6.

decisions.latin: In Deo laudábo verbum, in Dómino laudábo sermónem
decisions.why: D15 rules *verbum* and *sermo* both *palavra* and names 55:11 as a verse where the two stand side by side and 'decides locally'. Here the Greek differs too (ῥῆμα … λόγον), so by D15's own test the variation means something; but Portuguese has no plain second noun: *discurso* is a speech made, *fala* was refused three times by the Ps 118 stylist, *dito* is *elóquium*'s. Ruled for *palavra* twice: the verse's figure is the parallel (*In Deo laudábo … in Dómino laudábo …*), and it keeps the refrain whole — 55:5 *sermónes meos* and 55:6 *verba mea* are both *as minhas palavras* (both τοὺς λόγους μου in the Greek), so 55:11 still echoes 55:5. Cost, D15's accepted cost: the Latin's two nouns are one in Portuguese. The Lenten Gradual (Quad3-1) sings this verse. **v2:** the Latinist (minor) and the stylist both refused *a palavra … a palavra*: the Latin varies its noun, and the doubled word sounds like a copying slip. Taken, as the local decision D15 allows — the Greek differs here too, which is D15's own test. Of the two proposed nouns, the stylist's *a fala* (the thing spoken) over the Latinist's *o discurso* (a speech, heard as someone's oration). D15 refused *falas* in the plural with a possessive (*as vossas falas*, 118); the singular without one reads as the pair *palavra / fala*. Cost: 55:5 *sermónes meos* stays *as minhas palavras* (τοὺς λόγους, as 55:6 *verba*), so *sermo* has two Portuguese words in this psalm; the refrain's echo 55:5 / 55:11 still rests on *palavra*.

options.label: a fala
options.note: Ruling (v2); stylist v1. The Latin's two nouns, and the Greek's (ῥῆμα / λόγον).

options.label: a palavra
options.note: Draft 1; D15. Both the Latinist and the stylist heard the repetition as a slip.

options.label: o discurso
options.note: latinist v1; a speech made — heard as praising someone's speech.

options.label: a sua palavra
options.note: DRB 'his speech'; supplies a possessive the Latin lacks.

decisions.why: *exsecrári* is only here (grep; the noun 58:13); L&S 'to curse, execrate', with *detestor* and *abominor* as synonyms; the Greek ἐβδελύσσοντο is 'abhorred'. *abominar* is taken by *abominári* (5:7b, 118:163). *detestar* says abhorring, which the Greek confirms, and is plain; DRB 'detested'.

options.label: detestavam
options.note: Ruling; DRB; the Greek's sense.

options.label: execravam
options.note: the cognate; holds curse and abhor, but bookish.

options.label: amaldiçoavam
options.note: the Latin word's first classical sense; the Greek says abhor.

options.label: abominavam
options.note: MS1932; collides with *abominári*.

decisions.latin: advérsum me omnes cogitatiónes eórum in malum
decisions.why: A nominal clause; Portuguese needs a verb (D2). The imperfect follows *exsecrabántur* in the first colon (DRB 'were', MS1932 *eram*). Natural order, subject first. *cogitátio → pensamento* (row); *in malum → para o mal*. **v2:** the Latin order (*contra mim eram todos os seus pensamentos para o mal*), from the stylist: *para o mal* no longer trails after a comma. His present *são* refused — the first colon is past — and stays option 2.

options.label: eram
options.note: Ruling; DRB, MS1932.

options.label: são
options.note: a present state; the first colon is past.

decisions.why: Both Latin verbs are active and objectless (παροικήσουσιν καὶ κατακρύψουσιν): 'they will dwell and hide' — hide themselves, or hide (snares; cf. 9:16b, 30:5, 34:7 *abscondérunt láqueum*). Transitive *esconder* with no object is heard in Portuguese as a sentence cut off, so the reflexive is supplied as grammar (D2), as DRB 'hide themselves' and MS1932 *esconder-se-ão* do. *inhabitáre → habitar* (36:29). This is the one place the draft closes something the Latin leaves open; the bare verb is option 2 for the Latinist to weigh. **v2:** the Latinist marked the reflexive (minor) and asked for the bare verb; taken — it is the ambiguity the brief says to keep, and the ambiguity reader already heard the enemies lying hidden in draft 1.

options.label: esconderão
options.note: Ruling (v2); latinist v1: the Latin is active and objectless; the reflexive changed the voice and closed what it leaves open.

options.label: se esconderão
options.note: Draft 1; DRB, MS1932 — supplies the reflexive.

decisions.why: *observáre* a person with hostile intent → *espreitar* (open row, 36:12); the heel is kept, *calcáneum → calcanhar* (D43; 48:6). MS1932 *espiarão todos os meus passos* explains the image away. *ipsi* → *eles* (emphatic subject named).

options.label: espreitarão
options.note: Ruling; the row's word.

options.label: vigiarão
options.note: plainer; less hostile.

options.label: observarão
options.note: the cognate; neutral, and *serváre*'s word.

decisions.why: *sustinére* (ὑπέμειναν) with God as object is *esperar por* (D36); here the object is the psalmist's soul, and the waiting is the enemies' lying in wait for it. The same verb keeps the Latin's word; the hostility is in the context (55:7 *espreitarão*). *ánima mea → a minha alma* (row; *vida* is the idiom's sense and an option).

options.label: esperaram pela minha alma
options.note: Ruling; D36's verb; DRB 'waited for my soul'.

options.label: aguardaram a minha alma
options.note: *aguardar* is *exspectáre*'s (D36).

options.label: esperaram pela minha vida
options.note: MS1932 *tirar-me a vida*; the idiom's sense; the row keeps *alma*.

decisions.why: ὑπὲρ τοῦ μηθενὸς σώσεις αὐτούς: 'for nothing' — in no way, or for no price (DRB 'for nothing shalt thou save them'). *por nada* holds both, as the Latin does; MS1932 *de nenhum modo os salvarás* decides for the first. *salvum fácere → salvar* (row).

options.label: por nada
options.note: Ruling; DRB.

options.label: de nenhum modo
options.note: MS1932; decides the ambiguity.

decisions.why: The Latin has no possessive (30:10 *in ira* → *na ira*; 26:9 *com ira*); DRB and MS1932 supply 'thy'. Kept without. *confríngere → quebrar* (row; 2:9, 17:39).

options.label: na ira
options.note: Ruling; as the Latin.

options.label: na vossa ira
options.note: DRB, MS1932; supplies *tua*.

decisions.why: The colon is a versicle on its own (Psalmi matutinum [Daya3], Quad5-5: *V. Deus, vitam meam annuntiávi tibi. R. Posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo*, grep), so each half must read alone. *annuntiáre → anunciar* (D41). Natural order with the subject pronoun (D2).

options.label: eu vos anunciei a minha vida

forms.vitam: eu vos anunciei a minha vida

options.note: Ruling; natural order, cadence on *vida*.

options.label: a minha vida vos anunciei
options.note: the Latin's order; oxytone cadence.

decisions.why: The open row *in conspéctu* proposes *à vista de* (5:9, 9:20, 18:15a, 21:26); 40:13 and Ps 118 have *na vossa presença*. *pôr diante da vista* is the image here, of tears set where God sees them; *à vossa vista* follows the row.

options.label: à vossa vista
options.note: Ruling; the row.

options.label: diante de vós
options.note: plainest; drops the seeing.

decisions.latin: ecce, cognóvi, quóniam Deus meus es
decisions.why: The perfect of coming to know; 19:7a *nunc cognóvi* → *agora soube* after a Latinist major against the present. With a *que*-clause 118:75 has *Conheci, Senhor, que …*, which keeps the row's verb *conhecer*. *vós* named, so that *sois* is not left hanging after *eis*; DRB 'behold I know', MS1932 *logo conhecerei* (a future, not the Latin). **v2:** the stylist found *conheci que* not current and the bare *eis,* clipped; the ambiguity reader found the past after *em qualquer dia* jarring. Taken: *eis que* and *saber* (19:7a); the *quóniam*-clause said after a colon, which is how Portuguese says it. The perfect stays, as the Latin.

options.label: eis que eu soube: vós sois

forms.cognovi: eis que eu soube: vós sois

options.note: Ruling (v2); the stylist's build (*eis que eu sei: vós sois*) with the Latin's perfect kept (19:7a *agora soube*, where the present drew a Latinist major).

options.label: conheci
options.note: Draft 1 build; 118:75.

options.label: soube
options.note: 19:7a's verb.

options.label: eu sei

forms.cognovi: eis, eu sei que vós sois

options.note: DRB; the present, which drew a Latinist major at 19:7a.

options.label: eis que eu sei: vós sois

forms.cognovi: eis que eu sei: vós sois

options.note: stylist v1 as proposed; refused: the present (see 19:7a).

decisions.latin: In me sunt, Deus, vota tua
decisions.why: *vota tua* are the vows owed to God (made to you); *in me* — upon me as a debt, or within me. Both kept open: *Em mim estão … os vossos votos*. MS1932 explains (*A meu cuidado estão … os votos que te fiz*); the Hebrew עָלַי 'upon me' is not the Latin's preposition.

options.label: Em mim estão / os vossos votos
options.note: Ruling; DRB 'In me, O God, are vows to thee'.

options.label: Sobre mim estão / os vossos votos
options.note: the debt made explicit; the Hebrew's preposition.

options.label: Em mim estão / os votos que vos fiz
options.note: MS1932; explains *tua*.

decisions.why: The *erípere* row: *arrancar* where a *de …* names the source (53:9 *de toda tribulação me arrancastes*), *libertar* where none is named. Here there are two sources, death and the fall. Ps 114:8 (*erípuit ánimam meam de morte … pedes meos a lapsu*) should copy it. *lapsus → queda* (MS1932).

options.label: arrancastes
options.note: Ruling; the row.

options.label: livrastes
options.note: MS1932; *livrar* is *liberáre*'s neighbour.

decisions.why: *placére* (εὐαρεστῆσαι) → *agradar*, the *complacére* row's verb; *coram Deo* → *diante de Deus* (DRB 'in the sight of God'). *agradar diante de Deus* keeps both Latin words; MS1932 *seja agradável a Deus* drops *coram*. *vivéntium → dos vivos* (26:13 *na terra dos vivos*).

options.label: agrade
options.note: Ruling.

options.label: seja agradável
options.note: MS1932's build, with *diante de* kept.

decisions.why: *vota réddere → pagar os votos* (the réddere row; 21:26 *pagarei os meus votos*, finished). The stylist (v1) finds *pagar votos* commercial and asks *cumprir*; refused for the formula's sake — it recurs at 49:14, 60:9, 65:13, 115:5, 115:9, and *pagar* keeps the debt the Latin and Greek (ἀποδώσω) name; the ambiguity reader heard 'I will fulfil them by praising you' without trouble. His colon before the apposition taken (v2).

options.label: pagarei
options.note: Ruling; the row, 21:26.

options.label: cumprirei
options.note: stylist v1; MS1932 *cumprirei*. Would part from 21:26.

choices.55:2: *Miserére mei, Deus* → *Tende piedade de mim, Deus* (formula row; no *ó*: the Latin has none). The Lenten Gradual (Quad3-1, Quad5-1) sings this verse with *bellans*.
choices.55:4: *ego vero* → *eu, porém* (118:70). *timébo* (future) kept against MS1932's *Estou temendo*; 55:5's *não temerei* answers it.
choices.55:5: The refrain: 55:5 and 55:11 share *Em Deus louvarei … em Deus esperei … não temerei o que me faça …*; they differ where the Latin differs (*sermónes meos / verbum … sermónem*, *caro / homo*). *In Deo laudábo sermónes meos* kept as the Latin has it — 'in God I will praise my words' — against MS1932's gloss (*as palavras que me dirigiu*).
choices.55:6: *verba mea* → *as minhas palavras*, the same words as 55:5's *sermónes meos*: the Greek has τοὺς λόγους μου in both (D15).
choices.55:9b: *Sicut et* → *Assim como também*, as 55:8's *Sicut* → *Assim como*. *converténtur retrórsum* → *voltarão para trás* (the *retrórsum* row, which named 55:9). Natural order, subject before verb; the trailing colon of the DO text kept.
choices.55:10: *invocávero* (future perfect) → *em que vos invocar* (19:10 *no dia em que vos invocarmos*).
choices.55:12: *laudatiónes tibi* in apposition to *vota*, as the Latin (αἰνέσεως σοι); *réddere vota → pagar os votos* (row; 21:26). v2: a colon before the apposition, from the stylist.
choices.55:8: *fácies … confrínges* → *salvareis … quebrareis*: the stylist (v1) heard a chime of *-areis* across the asterisk; the Latin has the same echo (two futures in *-es*), so it is kept (rule 5). His move (*quebrareis na ira os povos*) would put the two futures side by side across the mediant. *por nada* keeps the Latin's open *pro níhilo*: the ambiguity reader heard it split between "in no way" and "freely" — so is the Latin (DRB "for nothing"); *de nenhum modo* stays option 2.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm55.txt, 13 prayed verses (55:2–55:13 with 55:9b); no flex, one mediant per verse; no titulus (D7). Liturgical uses (ps032/uses.py): 55:2, 55:11, 55:9 in the Gradual/Tract of Quad3-1 (with *bellans* and *sperábo*), 55:2 in Quad5-1; 55:9 the Wednesday Matins versicle (Psalmi matutinum [Daya3]) and Quad5-5; 55:10 in a Redemptorist antiphon and Quad6-3.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps055.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, DRB, MS1932; no Diurnal for this psalm). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Rulings applied: D2, D5 (not met), D15 (*palavra* for verbum/sermo, 55:11 decided locally), D24 (*o dia todo*), D36 (*esperar em*, *esperar por*), D41 (*anunciar*), D43 (*calcanhar*). Rows applied: conculcáre (*pisar aos pés*, the Ps 7 proposal), tribuláre, erípere, in conspéctu, retrórsum, réddere, observáre, cogitátio, confríngere, salvum fácere, invocáre, laudátio. The refrain copies 117:6 exactly (*não temerei o que me faça o homem*). Hard readings: 55:4 *ab altitúdine diéi*, 55:7 objectless *abscóndent*, 55:8 *pro níhilo*, 55:11 *verbum / sermónem*, 55:12 *In me … vota tua*.

Draft 1: hard pass. Two soft flags accepted: 55:10b −3 (*ecce, cognóvi, quóniam* is long in Latin; *eis, conheci que* is how Portuguese says it, *vós* already supplied) and 55:13a −3 (the Latin's *ánimam meam*, *pedes meos* are three syllables each against two). No rhyme flags. Oxytone cadences (*pés*, *atribulou*, *temerei*, *vós*, *esperei*, *mim*, *mal*, *esconderão*, *calcanhar*, *salvareis*, *trás*, *invocar*, *Deus*) are the Latin's words in plain order; allowed by rule 4.

claude-opus-5-5 (fresh context), the gate on draft 2. No major; two minors, both refused with reasons below (both are options). He approved the kept hard spots (*Da altura do dia*, the objectless *esconderão*, *os vossos votos*, the elliptical 55:9b) and the pointing.

outcomes.remark: *quóniam* turned into a colon; *soube* narrower than *cognóvi* → *eis que conheci que vós sois o meu Deus*
outcomes.reason: his own note calls both defensible; draft 1's *conheci que* was refused by the v1 stylist as not current and the bare *eis,* as clipped; *soube* is the verb 19:7a took for *cognóvi* + *quóniam* after a Latinist major. *eis, conheci que vós sois* stays option 2.

outcomes.remark: *sermónes* → *palavras* blurs sermo / verbum → *as minhas falas*
outcomes.reason: D15 rules sermo → palavra and refused the plural *falas* (the Ps 118 stylist, three times); 55:5 *sermónes meos* and 55:6 *verba mea* are the same Greek (τοὺς λόγους μου), so there the Latin's variation carries no sense; 55:11 took *fala* only because the Greek differs there too (ῥῆμα / λόγον) and both v1 readers heard the doubled noun as a slip.
